label: R4
title: Review: Parts VII and VIII – particles, comparisons, can and should, causatives and passives
summary: The book's review exercises on word order with ba and other particles, comparing and intensifying adjectives, can/should sentences, magpa- and pa- + -in verbs, plural adjectives, verbs and adjectives used as nouns, and passive sentences, with the book's answers
goals: Put ba, raw, rin, pô, na and pa in the right place
Say good, very good, how good and most industrious
Compare people and things: more than, as … as, of the same height
Say what someone can, should or needs to do
Understand magpa- and pa- + -in sentences, plural adjectives, and ang + verb or adjective

blocks.t: This lesson is the book's own **review exercises, Parts VII and VIII**. Every item is copied exactly as the book prints it. After each exercise you will find **the book's answer** from its answer key (the book gives no answer for the two *create sentences* exercises).

blocks.title: How to use this review
items: Say or write your own answer first. Then compare it with the book's answer.
Each exercise names the lesson to **revise** if you find it hard.
The exercises at the end of this lesson are built from the book's answers.

sections.title: Part VII A. Put the words in order

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Arrange the words and particles in the following sentences, and replace with correct ones.

head: As printed
rows: marumi ang bata ang raw ba
siya ay kumain rin ay ba po
bakit siya hindi makatatakbo nang mabilis

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. Marumi raw ba ang bata?
2. Siya ba ay bata pa?
3. Siya rin pô ba ay kumain?
4. Nakaalis na ba siya?
5. Hindi pa siya nakapag-aral.
6. Bakit hindi siya makatakbo ng mabilis?
7. Ito ba ang aklat mo?

blocks.title: Particles follow the first word
blocks.note: The book's answers to items 1 and 4.

blocks.t: As Lesson 10 showed, little words such as **na, pa, rin, raw** and **pô** come after the question word or the predicate and push **ba** further back. **Raw** means *they say*; **rin** means *too, also*; **pa** means *still, yet*; **na** means *already*.

blocks.title: Book slips
items: Item 4 prints **nab a**: a misprint for **na ba**.
Items 1 and 3 have an extra word (a second **ang**, a second **ay**) that the answer drops.
Item 6: the answer also changes **makatatakbo** to **makatakbo** and **nang** to **ng**.
Item 3 prints **po**; the answer prints **pô**.

blocks.title: Revise
blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 10 (The question word ba).

sections.title: Part VII B. Good, very good, most industrious

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Give the Tagalog equivalent of the following words and phrases.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. good - **mabuti**
2. very good - **napakabuti**
3. how good - **kay buti** or **mabuting-mabuti**
4. industrious - **masipag**
5. very industrious - **napakasipag** or **masipag na masipag**
6. most industrious - **pinakamasipag**.

head: mabuti (good)
masipag (industrious)
blocks.title: The book's answer as a table
blocks.note: napaka- = very; pinaka- = most; an adjective doubled with a ligature (masipag na masipag) is also very.

blocks.title: Book spellings
items: Lesson 11 writes **nápaka-** with an accent; this answer key prints **napaka-**.
Lesson 41 writes **kaybúti** (how good!) as one word; this answer key prints **kay buti**.
Lesson 11 gives a doubled adjective (magandáng-magandá) as *very*; here the book gives **mabuting-mabuti** for *how good*.

blocks.title: Revise
blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 11 (Making comparisons).
**Book's instruction:** Translate these sentences into Tagalog.

head: English
rows: John is taller than his brother.
My house is as beautiful as his.
His child is smaller than my child.
His child is of the same height as mine.
His dog is not as bad as his neighbor's.
Jack and his friend are of the same color.
My sister is more beautiful than I.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. Lalong marunong si Peter kaysa kay John.
2. Lalong mataas si John kaysa sa kanyang kapatid na lalaki.
3. Ang aking bahay ay kasingganda ng kaniyang bahay.
4. Maliit ang kanyang anak.
5. Lalong maliit ang kanyang anak kaysa sa anak ko.
6. Magkasintaas ang anak niya at ang anak ko.
7. Ang kanyang aso ay hindi kasinsama ng aso ng kapitbahay niya.
8. Magkapatid sina John at Peter.
9. Si Jack at ang kanyang kaibigan ay magkasingkulay.
10. Lalong maganda ang aking kapatid kaysa sa akin.

blocks.title: More than: lalong + adjective + kaysa
blocks.note: Kaysa kay before a person's name; kaysa sa before other nouns (Lesson 11).

blocks.title: Which word for which idea?
items: *more … than*: **lalong** + adjective + **kaysa kay / kaysa sa** (items 1, 2, 5, 10).
*as … as*: **kasing-** / **kasin-** + root (kasingganda, kasinsama) (items 3, 7).
*of the same …* for two people together: **magkasin-** / **magkasing-** (magkasintaas, magkasingkulay) (items 6, 9).
*brothers*: **magkapatid** (item 8).

blocks.title: Book spellings
blocks.t: Item 3 prints **kaniyang**; the other answers print **kanyang**. Lesson 11 writes lalóng, káysa and kasíng- with accents; this answer key prints them without.

sections.title: Part VII E. Can, should, need

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Translate the following into Tagalog.

head: English
rows: Why don't you eat your supper?

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. Huwag kang kumain ngayon.
2. Hindi siya marunong sumakay sa kabayo.
3. Marunong ka bang lumangoy?
4. Oo, marunong akong lumangoy.
5. Kailangan mong mag-aral ng Tagalog araw-araw.
6. Bakit hindi ka kumain ng iyong hapunan?
7. Alam mo ba ang kanyang pangalan?
8. Ano ang kailangan mo?

blocks.title: Notice
items: Here *can swim* and *cannot ride* are said with **marunong** followed by the verb in the infinitive: **marunong akong lumangoy**, **marunong sumakay**.
Item 5 uses **Kailangan mong** (*you need to*) for *you should*.
**Huwag kang** + infinitive = *don't* (Lesson 37).
**Ba** goes after **ka** and **mo**: *Marunong ka bang…?*, *Alam mo ba…?* (Lesson 10).

blocks.title: Revise
blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 17 (Pseudo verbs) and Lesson 37 (huwág).

sections.title: Part VIII A. Create sentences with pa- + -in and magpa-

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Create sentences from the following root words using the prefixes on the left. Afterwards, give the English translation of your sentences.

blocks.title: Your turn
items: 1. **lambót** using **pa-in**
2. **kain** using **magpa-**
3. **upo** using **pa_in**
4. **inom** using **magpa-**
The book gives no single answer for this exercise. Look at Part VIII B for model sentences.

blocks.t: Remember from Lesson 36: **magpa-** and **pa- + -in** verbs are about having something done: someone gives an order to have something done to another. **Magpa-** is active; **pa- + -in** is passive.

blocks.title: Book slip
blocks.t: Item 3 prints **pa_in** (an underscore): it means **pa-in**, as in item 1.

blocks.title: Revise
blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 36 (Magpa- and pa- + -in verb forms).

sections.title: Part VIII B. Made to do it: into English

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Translate the following sentences into English.

head: Tagalog
rows: Ang kanyang tákot ay nagpatakbó kay Juan.

items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. Don't tear the paper.
2. I made him/her write a letter.
3. His father made him/her leave.
4. His fear made Juan run.
5. He/She made me read the newspaper.

sections.title: Part VIII C. Plural adjectives two ways

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Give the plural form of the following adjectives in two ways.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. **magaganda**; **mga maganda**
2. **mabubuti**; **mga mabuti**

blocks.t: Way 1 is the one from Lesson 4: repeat the first syllable of the root (ma**ga**ganda, ma**bu**buti). Way 2 puts **mga** in front of the adjective.

blocks.title: Book spellings
blocks.t: The exercise prints **magandá**; the answer prints magaganda and mga maganda without accents. Lesson 4 writes **magagandá**.

blocks.title: Revise
blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 4 (Plurals: mga and plural adjectives).

sections.title: Part VIII D. Ang + adjective or verb: into English

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Translate the following phrases into English.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. the good one
2. the good man
3. the one reading
4. the thing being read
5. the manner of running or the running of (something such as a contest)
6. the washing of clothes

blocks.t: As in Lesson 31, putting **ang** in front of an adjective or a verb turns it into a noun: **ang mabaít** is *the good one*. Compare item 3, an active verb (*the one reading*), with item 4, a passive -in verb (*the thing being read*).

blocks.title: Book slip
blocks.t: Item 3 prints **and bumábasa**: a misprint for **ang bumábasa**.

blocks.title: Revise
blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 31 (Forming nouns).

sections.title: Part VIII E. Passive sentences: into English

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Translate the following sentences into English using the passive voice of verbs.

head: Tagalog
rows: Ako'y kanyang binigyán ng aklát niya.
Ang iyong ibinigay ay akin na.
Ang sa kanyá ay hindi magagámit ng ibá.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. I was saved by him.
2. He was hit by his friend.
3. He had not written to me.
4. His/her book was given to me by him.
5. What you have given me is mine already.
6. What is his/hers cannot be used by another.

blocks.title: Passive in English
items: In items 1 to 4 the one who receives the action is the subject (**ako**, **siya**), and the doer is in the possessive form (**kanyáng**, **ng kaibigan niya**, **niya**, **kanyang**).
Item 3: the book's English (*He had not written to me*) is not in the passive voice.

blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 15 (-in- verb forms), Lesson 32 (I- verb forms) and Lesson 33 (-An verb forms).

recap: Particles follow the first word and push ba back: Marumi raw ba ang bata? Nakaalis na ba siya?
mabuti, napakabuti, kay buti / mabuting-mabuti; masipag, napakasipag / masipag na masipag, pinakamasipag.
More than: Lalong marunong si Peter kaysa kay John. As … as: kasingganda. Same height: magkasintaas.
Can: marunong + -ng + infinitive (Marunong ka bang lumangoy?). Need/should: Kailangan mong mag-aral.
Made someone do it: Pinasulat ko siya ng liham. Plurals: magaganda / mga maganda. Ang + verb or adjective = a noun.
